name: Sergeant Darryn

facts.text: Every named of the Hall takes no damage once drawn past its tether, and walks back to its post.

story:
The voice. Sergeant Darryn ran the watchmen of the hall's west passage, and ran them hard, with a voice that the reports say could be heard through two doors. He was the loudest man in the hall and proud of it; Lady Darra used to say she could tell the hour by which of his men he was shouting at. Like every officer of the Pennine watch, it is bound to its post: one step past where its captain stood it, no blow lands and it walks home at full health. Fight it where it stands. 

The watchmen still answer that voice. He is not strong as the captains are strong, but where Darryn stands the restless watchmen stand thicker, called by the shout that once got them out of their bunks. He holds his corner of the hall as if Lord Gildas might come round on inspection at any moment, and he still shouts at his men to stand straight, though they have been dead for longer than most raiders have been alive. The bards say that his shouting is the reason the Silencer of Caer Sidi would hate the Pennine watch, if it ever heard of it.

The reports say he had a son in Camelot whom he wrote to every month, loudly, so that the clerk could hear every word through the door and set them down if the sergeant asked. The last letter is in the clerk's hand, unfinished, on the table of the captains' hall. It tells the boy to stand straight and mind his mother. It does not say goodbye.
legend: A sergeant with five thousand health and a crowd of restless watchmen around him who answer his shout. Clear the watchmen around his post first, then drop him fast where he stands. Do not drag him into the corridor; he will not take a scratch there and will walk back with his voice still going. He hits no harder than a living sergeant would. The danger is purely the watchmen he calls. The watchmen around him are restless watchmen: soft one by one, deadly in a crowd. Area damage first, then the sergeant, then rest before the stair.

loremasterTopic.text: Sergeant Darryn ran the watchmen of the Hall's west passage, and ran them hard, with a voice that the last reports say could be heard through two doors.

bookPage: Sergeant Darryn has been shouting since dawn. He says the watchmen of the west passage are slack, and that a doubled watch is twice as many men to be slack, and that he will not have it. I can hear him through two doors as I write. The Lady Darra says she can tell the hour by which man he is shouting at. Tonight, after the trouble on the road, he went quiet for the first time in all my years here, and the quiet was worse than the shouting. In the morning he was shouting again, and we were all, I think, relieved.
